content:
kevin: Heads up — hosted API p95/p99 spiked around 10:20 UTC. p95 went from ~180ms to ~720ms, p99 > 2s. No obvious node OOMs. Filing here to triage, tagging @samir and runtime folks :eyes:

samir: On it. Which routes/models affected? Any correlation with traffic?

kevin: Mostly text-gen endpoints for medium-length requests (seq ~512). Traffic increased ~15% but not enough to explain 4x p95. No rate-limit errors in logs.

maria: Quick look at the request queues — frontend LB queue depth jumped from ~5 to ~60 concurrent waiting requests at the same time p95 rose. Worker grpc queue length shows backlog. Metrics snippet: `queue_depth{service="hosting-router"} 60 -> 6` and `worker_backlog{pool="shared-gpu"} 70 -> 4` after the spike.

jin: Also saw a KV cache miss rate spike (miss_rate from 3% -> 22%). Eviction rate also up. Suspect KV cache thrash causing extra backend fetches and longer tails.

elaine: Any kernel selection churn? I remember a recent change where the runtime falls back to a generic kernel when sequence shapes mismatch. If that fallback kicked in we'd see tail latency.

jin: I grabbed a short perf/profile from a busy worker during the spike:
```
# perf top excerpt
 25.1%  runtime_kernel_generic
 17.6%  kv_fetch_sync
 11.3%  scheduler_spin
  9.8%  cuda_memcpy_async_wait
```
That aligns with generic kernel plus blocking KV fetches.

samir: Interesting. Two possible amplifiers: (1) batching heuristics produced larger batches -> higher latency under contention, (2) KV misses forcing sync disk reads or remote redis calls. Any evidence batching changed?

maria: Batching logs around the window show an uptick in batch assemble time and some large batches hitting the GPU: `batch_size_histogram buckets: 1: 30% | 8: 50% | 32: 20%` before the spike. At spike onset, we saw more 32-sized batches. Looks like a short-lived routing change sent more requests to the shared pool.

kevin: Routing change? We did a small policy tweak hours earlier to prefer lower-cost pools for small models — could have been mis-routed.

elaine: If large batches plus generic kernel fallback occur, the effective per-request latency increases significantly (queueing + kernel slow path). We should check kernel selection logs: `kernel_selector.decisions` shows fallbacks when sequence_len % 64 != 0.

jin: Pulled kernel-selection trace: several models had shape (seq=510) which triggered fallback to generic kernels because our optimized kernel expects multiples of 64. That explains overhead.

samir: So chain is: routing -> concentration on shared pool -> larger batches -> sequence shapes not aligned -> kernel fallback -> longer GPU time -> frontend queues grow -> KV cache thrash magnifies tail.

kevin: Agreed. Immediate mitigation options? Reduce batch_target for shared pool, pin hot routes to dedicated pools, and increase KV cache headroom.

elaine: I pushed a temporary config to reduce max_batch_size from 32 -> 8 for the shared-gpu pool: `rtctl set pool.shared-gpu.max_batch_size=8 --sticky 30m`

infra-bot: deploy/rollout started for config rtctl set pool.shared-gpu.max_batch_size=8 (change-id: cfg-2026-03-18-145)

maria: After the change, queue depth fell from 60 -> 8 within 90s, p95 dropped back to ~200ms and p99 under 900ms. KV miss rate normalized.

jin: Follow-up items: (a) add telemetry to flag kernel fallback rates per model, (b) adjust kernel selection to allow padding for seq lengths near optimized widths, (c) make routing respect model shape distribution to avoid concentrating bad-shape requests into one pool.

samir: I'll open a short incident doc and a prioritized task list. We should also consider temporarily increasing KV cache quota for the shared pool to reduce eviction storms.

kevin: Thanks everyone. Marking this thread resolved for now — we'll track the follow-ups in a small epic. :white_check_mark:
